problem:
Given that ${y}_{0}(x)=x$ is a particular solution of the Riccati differential equation

$$
{y}^{′}=-x\,{y}^{2}+2{x}^{2}y+1-{x}^{3}
$$

find the general solution of the equation.
worked_solution:
The equation

$$
{y}^{′}=-x\,{y}^{2}+2{x}^{2}y+1-{x}^{3},
$$

is a Riccati differential equation of the form

$$
{y}^{′}=a(x){y}^{2}+b(x)y+c(x),
$$

where

$$
a(x)=-x,\,b(x)=2{x}^{2},\,c(x)=1-{x}^{3}.
$$

To reduce the given Riccati equation to a Bernoulli equation, we use the substitution

$$
y(x)=z(x)+{y}_{0}(x),
$$

where ${y}_{0}(x)$ is a known particular solution.
Differentiating gives

$$
{y}^{′}(x)={z}^{′}(x)+{y}_{0}^{′}(x).
$$

In our case, ${y}_{0}(x)=x.$ Since ${y}_{0}^{′}(x)=1$, we have

$$
y=z+x\,⇒\,{y}^{′}={z}^{′}+1.
$$

Let's substitute these expressions into our Riccati equation:

$$
{z}^{′}+1=-x\,(z+x)^{2}+2{x}^{2}(z+x)+1-{x}^{3}.
$$

Now, we expand the right-hand side, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{′}+1 & =-x({z}^{2}+2xz+{x}^{2})+2{x}^{2}z+2{x}^{3}+1-{x}^{3} \\ {z}^{′}+1 & =-x{z}^{2}+1 \\ {z}^{′} & =-x{z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve the obtained equation using separation of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =-x{z}^{2} \\ \frac{1}{{z}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =-x \\ \int \frac{1}{{z}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int -x\,\text{d}x \\ \int {z}^{-2}\,\text{d}z & =\int -x\,\text{d}x \\ -\frac{1}{z} & =-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+C \\ z & =\frac{2}{{x}^{2}+C}\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

Finally, let's substitute $z=y-x$ to recover the initial variable $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\frac{2}{{x}^{2}+C} \\ y-x & =\frac{2}{{x}^{2}+C} \\ y & =x+\frac{2}{{x}^{2}+C}\end{aligned}
$$
